declarations.description:
Author renders entries as `<article data-activity>` children, each carrying
its timestamp either as `data-time="ISO"` or as an authored
`<time datetime="ISO">` direct child (which also gives a no-JS time).
Component:
  - Decorates each entry with a relative-time badge (upgrading an authored
    `<time>` in place, or creating one from data-time)
  - Optionally groups entries under day / week date headings (data-group)
  - Optionally renders a left-rail avatar / icon (data-activity-avatar /
    data-activity-icon)
  - Wires the WAI-ARIA Feed pattern: role="feed", aria-labelledby /
    aria-describedby per article, aria-posinset / aria-setsize (-1 while
    more may load), aria-busy around load-more, keyboard nav
    (PageDown / PageUp, Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End; Arrow / Home / End when the
    article itself has focus)
  - Optionally arms an IntersectionObserver sentinel for infinite scroll
    (data-infinite → activity-feed:load-more event with a done() callback)
  - Watches for new direct children via MutationObserver and decorates them

Accessibility tree: date headings, the sentinel and the empty-state text are
DOM children of the host, but only <article>s are feed children. Headings
and the sentinel are aria-hidden (a heading's text is attached to the first
article of its group via aria-describedby); while the feed is empty the host
role is "group" so the empty-state paragraph is a legitimate child.

Read-only / immutable per entry — distinct from `<comment-thread>`
(mutable + threaded) and `<chat-thread>` (real-time, sender-grouped).

declarations.description: Decide whether data may be written to an attribute.

Security:
- Only simple property paths are allowed - no expressions, methods, or
  template literals.
- data-field-html is passed through the shared sanitizer.
- data-field-attr refuses event-handler attributes (on*, plus srcdoc and
  style) and only writes URL-bearing attributes (href, src, action,
  formaction, xlink:href, poster, cite, background, ping, data, srcset)
  when the URL is http(s), mailto, tel, relative, or a fragment.

Attributes:
- src: URL to fetch JSON data from
- data-items: Inline JSON data
- data-key: Property to use as unique key for items (falls back to the
  item index when the key is missing or duplicated)
- data-loading / data-error: state reflected by the component

Binding Attributes (on elements inside the template):
- data-field="path" - Set textContent from property path
- data-field-attr="href: url, title: name" - Set attributes from property
  paths; null/undefined (or false, except aria-*) removes the attribute,
  true sets it empty (boolean attributes)
- data-field-html="richContent" - Set innerHTML (sanitized)
- data-field-if="propertyPath" - Hidden unless truthy
- data-field-unless="propertyPath" - Hidden when truthy

Children with [data-fallback] are static no-JS content, removed on the
first successful render.

declarations.description:
Wires chat-thread, chat-input, participant data, and an optional model
selector into a composed shell. Handles the send → typing → response cycle.

Transport: when `endpoint` is set, uses built-in fetch(). When omitted,
dispatches `chat-window:send` so consumers can provide their own transport.
In both cases, the typing indicator is shown while awaiting a response.
Custom transports finish it with `resolveTyping(typingElement, html)`.
The built-in transport POSTs `{ message, model }` — the latest message
only, no history — and reads `html`, `message` or `content` from the JSON
reply. An in-flight request is aborted when the element disconnects.

Content trust: user-typed text is always inserted as text (never parsed
as HTML). Agent/system content and endpoint replies are HTML, passed
through sanitizeToFragment() (nodes inserted, never re-parsed).

Participants: the `data-participants` JSON map uses arbitrary string IDs.
The local user's messages are always created with `data-from="user"`.
The agent is resolved as the first participant with `role: "agent"`.
Override these defaults by choosing matching keys in your participant map.

Model: `model` is a property + attribute. Setting the property updates the
`<select data-model-select>` if present. The attribute is set at connect
time and updated when the select changes. There is no `observedAttributes`
— post-connect attribute mutations are not observed; use the property setter.

Submit / Cancel button row. Used standalone for top-level comment forms or
as the reply-form template inside <comment-thread>.

Presentational with respect to persistence: the component fires
`comment-box:submit` and lets the author make the network call. The
submit contract (dispatch is synchronous, so decide during the handler):

  - Do nothing → the value clears right after the event.
  - Call `e.detail.waitUntil(promise)` → the box goes busy (aria-busy,
    Submit aria-disabled, editor read-only) until the promise settles.
    Resolve → the value clears. Reject → the value is kept for a retry.
  - Call `e.preventDefault()` synchronously → the value is kept and the
    box does nothing more; call `clear()` yourself when appropriate.

`preventDefault()` after an `await` is too late — the event has finished
dispatching. Use waitUntil() for async work.

positioned over the grid, re-measured on resize, laid out in columns when
they overlap, and marked data-continues when they run past the last row.

declarations.description:
Fetches remote HTML and injects it into the element. Progressive enhancement:
any existing content is shown as a fallback until the fetch completes.

Security model (safe by default):
- Same-origin only. `src` is resolved against document.baseURI; only
  http(s) URLs on the page's origin load. blob:, data:, javascript:, file:
  and other schemes are always refused. Other origins need the explicit
  `allow-cross-origin` attribute (and that server's CORS consent). A
  same-origin URL that redirects off-origin is refused the same way.
- Fetched HTML is sanitized (src/lib/sanitize-html.js) unless the author
  sets `trusted`. Nested <include-file>s keep their `src` but lose any
  trust attributes, so they stay same-origin + sanitized.
- Scripts in the fragment only run with BOTH `trusted` and `allow-scripts`.
  `allow-scripts` alone is ignored (with a console warning).
- Nesting: an include whose URL already appears in its ancestor
  <include-file> chain (A→B→A, or self) is refused, as is nesting deeper
  than MAX_DEPTH. Both surface as the normal error state.
- Relative URLs inside a fragment resolve against the host page, not the
  fragment's URL (the markup is parsed into the host document).

on every debounced keystroke.

declarations.description:
Owns field-level validation timing (validate when focus leaves the field,
then eagerly re-validate on every edit once an error has been shown) and
exposes a public API for the form coordinator.

Markup pattern:
  <form-field>
    <label for="name">Name</label>
    <input id="name" required
           data-message-valuemissing="Please enter your name" />
    <output class="hint" for="name">As it appears on your ID.</output>
    <output class="error" for="name" aria-live="polite"></output>
  </form-field>

The bound control is the first form-associated custom element inside the
field (date-picker, star-rating, combo-box …) or, failing that, the first
native input / textarea / select. Radio controls bind their whole group
(every radio sharing the name in the same form).

ARIA wiring done here: aria-describedby on the control lists the hint
output(s) and the textarea counter, then the error output while the field
is invalid (author ids are kept); aria-invalid mirrors the state. Ids are
generated for outputs that lack one. aria-errormessage is not used —
screen-reader support is still too uneven to rely on.

declarations.description:
A platform-native markdown viewer that resolves content from four slot types
(in priority order): `src` attribute, `<script type="text/markdown">`,
`<template data-md>`, or `<pre>` (recommended for progressive enhancement).

The default parser is the vendored `marked` (src/vendor/marked) with GFM
and VB callout blocks (`:::note|info|tip|warning|danger [title]` … `:::`).
Supply a custom parser via the `.parser` property to bypass it entirely.

Trust boundary: parsed HTML (from marked or a custom `.parser`) is passed
through the shared sanitizer (src/lib/sanitize-html.js, untrusted profile)
and the cleaned nodes are inserted directly — never serialised and parsed
again. Sanitising is ON by default because the viewer renders model output
(ai-summary) and user comments (comment-box → markdown-editor).
`sanitize="off"` writes the parser output with innerHTML: only for fully
trusted first-party markdown, and never together with a cross-origin or
user-influenced `src`.

`src` is same-origin by default (http(s) only, redirects re-checked);
`allow-cross-origin` opts in to other origins — the same policy as
`<include-file>`.

declarations.description:
Joins two data sources:
  - vocabulary.json (SKOS ConceptScheme) — provides the @id graph
    with skos:broader / skos:narrower / skos:hasTopConcept edges and
    skos:prefLabel display strings.
  - pages.json — each page record exposes `concepts: [id, …]` (harvested
    by generate-pages-json.js from repeated <meta name="concept"> tags
    per meta-tag-contract v1.1).

The component renders a nested <details>/<summary>/<ul> tree rooted at
the scheme's top concepts. Each node shows the concept's prefLabel, a
count of pages tagged with that concept OR any descendant, and links
to /topics/{id}/. Pages tagged with concepts not present in the
vocabulary land under "Uncategorized".

The tree degrades to native disclosure widgets without JavaScript;
only the data fetch + tree build are JS-driven.
declarations.name: TopicMap
